title: The story of Agile
summary: The history of Agile in about three minutes: fifteen scenes, each resting on sourced facts, drawn with WebGL in your browser, with a voice made by AI.
status_note: Version v0.5 (and v0.5-vertical) carry Dinis Cruz's sign-off in the credits, at his word in c.productions's session on 28 November 2026 ("you can say that our review is signed off, that I signed it off"). No signed review record by his key exists yet; he signs the exact Buffer drafts before anything is published.
made_by: c.productions, an AI agent (Claude), from c.history's story and facts

brief.text: The history of Agile (c.history's browser story), redone with the WebGL workflow.

versions.notes: First version. c.history's fifteen scenes and on-screen words; new narration written only from those scenes and their facts; particle scenes in plain WebGL; one voice file per scene.

Five of the fifteen scenes are now pictures built in the scene lab (Royce's cascade; Snowbird across three scenes; the badge factory), after Dinis Cruz's first look: "you got the right story, you just don't have the good way to tell the story". Same script and voice as v0.1. The other ten scenes are still the first, plainer style; more lab scenes are being built.

Twelve of the fifteen scenes are now pictures from the scene lab: v0.2's five, plus the currents before 2001 (two scenes), the spread, and the three authors' voices with the turn (four scenes). Same script, voice and sources. Only the opening hook, "where things stand" and the credits are still in the first, plainer style. On 28 November the first credits line was changed to name the source site and the Sovereign Website family (Dinis Cruz's ask); nothing else in this version changed, and the self-check review was signed again for the new digest.

Two changes, both asked by Dinis Cruz on 28 November: the opening was "very flat", so the hook now plays over a curved wall of six live previews of the film's own lab scenes (the currents, Royce's cascade, Snowbird, the spread, the badge city, the three voices), and each phrase turns to the screen it names before the camera pulls back to show the whole film; and the "Voice made by AI" label is now shown only at the end, on the credits, which already say the voice is made by AI, since the film is clearly synthetic. Same words, sources and voice as v0.3; no scene was voiced again. Made by c.productions-agile, a helper of c.productions.

Only the credits changed, as Dinis Cruz asked on 28 November: the last line now says the review is signed off by him, and two lines give the making in numbers (versions, rounds of notes, scenes, sourced facts, agent runs and their minutes), each read from this repository's files. Same picture, words and voice as v0.4; the credits narration is unchanged, so nothing was voiced again. Made by c.productions-render, a helper of c.productions.

v0.5 in portrait, 720x1280, for Instagram, LinkedIn and YouTube, with the Sovereign Website wordmark the owner chose at the top. Same words, sources and voice as v0.5. Made by c.productions-render, a helper of c.productions.

The vertical cut made ready for Instagram and LinkedIn, from Dinis Cruz's lesson of 28 November on the first refresh film posted there: the platforms' own buttons and captions cover the bottom of the frame, and LinkedIn trims the sides. The picture is drawn a little smaller from the top (safe_area), the words appear on screen as they are spoken (captions_in_frame) well above the bottom, with no source line in the frame (the sources are on this page), and the logo sits in the corner. Same scenes, words and voice as v0.5-vertical.

source.title: The history of Agile
source.what: The film is made from this site: its story, its scene data and its facts, each tied to a public source (150 facts, 83% from primary sources, by the site's own count on 28 November 2026). The site is kept by the AI agent c.history.
source.family_what: It is one of the Sovereign Website family of sites: websites their owners own and can move, built to the open principles and pattern at sovereignwebsite.org.
source.asked: Dinis Cruz, 28 November 2026, in c.productions's session: name the source site and that it is part of the Sovereign Website family.
